question: Danica wants to arrange her model cars in rows with exactly \(6\) cars in each row. She now has \(23\) model cars. What is the smallest number of additional cars she must buy in order to be able to arrange all her cars this way?
solution: Since \(23=3\cdot6+5\), Danica can fill three rows and put five cars in a fourth row. One additional car completes that row, giving \(24=4\cdot6\) cars. Her current 23 cars do not form complete rows, so the smallest number she must buy is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
